audit_findings.title: Current share count may be paired with stale interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt principal increased $306.673 million from FY2025 year-end to June 2026; at the filed 5.6% effective rate, computed annual interest is $17.173 million. Treating the full pretax amount as an OE reduction lowers base value by about $4.69 per share and the buy-below threshold from $72.44 to about $69.16.
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental interest reduces equity-level owner earnings; the later reduced share count affects the per-share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: These purchases were funded by our operating cash flows, as well as a $250 million expansion of our credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital-structure date mismatch is demonstrated, although the exact after-tax interest adjustment is unresolved. A conservative screen deducting the full computed pretax interest still leaves the adjusted buy-below threshold about $11.50 above the $57.66 market price, so this finding alone is not reasonably capable of reversing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Recast owner earnings using the June 2026 debt tranches, hedge rates, tax effect, and current fully diluted shares, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: MOVEit litigation may exceed the amount already accrued
audit_findings.mechanism: Any loss, defense cost, or deductible exceeding the recorded reserve would reduce future owner earnings or require an equity-value bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: While we are unable to predict the ultimate outcome of any of the remaining proceedings, we have accrued an amount within a range of possible outcomes expected to be incurred to resolve the matters.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending litigation and an existing accrual are demonstrated, but the reserve, possible-loss range, insurance recovery, and defense costs are undisclosed. The record therefore establishes a present exposure but cannot establish whether the unreserved amount is material to the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the reserve balance, reasonably possible excess-loss range, insurance limits and deductibles, expected defense costs, and the amount already reflected in the $375.2 million anchor; rerun for the uncovered excess.

audit_findings.title: Historical growth spans a changing business perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: The base-to-bear valuation difference is $20.36 per share; applying the 30% margin of safety to the $83.12 bear value gives $58.18, only $0.52 above the $57.66 price.
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-comparable historical owner earnings can distort the growth rate and trend used to select scenario growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: We have divested a number of businesses from this segment across fiscal years 2024 and 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The changing perimeter is demonstrated, while its net bias is unresolved because disposed or acquired operations may have different profitability. This is material: moving from 4% base growth to the existing 0% bear case reduces the margin-of-safety threshold from $72.44 to $58.18 and nearly eliminates the purchase-price cushion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2025 owner earnings on the current-company perimeter for all named acquisitions and disposals, reassess growth, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may contain episodic disaster-response earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Fiscal 2026 nine-month disaster-recovery revenue declined $83.289 million, equal to 3.6% of the prior-year federal segment revenue for that period; the associated profit and owner-earnings contribution are unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-cycle FEMA volumes, assessment activity, or reduced penalties could inflate normalized anchor owner earnings and the cash flows projected from it.
audit_findings.evidence: We have long-standing arrangements with FEMA to provide short-term assistance for natural disasters, the extent and timing of which are difficult to predict.
audit_findings.explanation: The later filing demonstrates that short-term disaster-recovery revenue did not recur to the same extent, but it does not isolate FY2025 FEMA profit, assessment-volume profit, or the penalty benefit. Federal segment operating income nevertheless increased $40.533 million in the nine-month comparison, so the record does not establish that the $375.2 million anchor is materially overstated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain FY2025 FEMA revenue and contribution profit, incremental assessment profit, and reduced-penalty benefit; remove only the above-cycle after-tax OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring $39.5 million disposal charge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed charge of $39.549 million, or 10.5% of the $375.2 million anchor; if retained, the computed base-value effect is approximately $587.2 million or $10.80 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining a nonrecurring disposal charge reduces normalized owner earnings; removing recurring indemnification cash payments incorrectly would have the opposite effect.
audit_findings.evidence: Our SG&A expenses for fiscal year 2025 include a charge of $39.5 million related to the sale of certain of our businesses in our Outside the U.S. Segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the anchor is not. The cash-flow statement adds back the same $39.549 million, indicating it did not reduce reported operating cash flow. If the OE calculation nevertheless retained it through an earnings-based path, its quantified scale is material and would substantially increase estimated value.
audit_findings.action: Trace every component of the $375.2 million anchor, confirm treatment of the $21.3 million currency reclassification and $11.3 million indemnification, retain recurring cash obligations, and rerun if any nonrecurring charge remains.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not all be freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: The entire bridge addition is $56.953 million, equal to a maximum $1.05 per share of intrinsic value and about $0.73 per share of the 30%-MOS buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.mechanism: Remittance taxes, penalties, restrictions, or working-capital requirements reduce the cash amount added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: When we are unable to remit funds back without incurring a penalty, we will consider these funds indefinitely reinvested until such time as these restrictions are changed.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of foreign remittance constraints is demonstrated, but the restricted portion of the latest balance is not. Even removing the entire $56.953 million bridge balance would leave the buy-below threshold near $71.71, approximately $14.05 above the $57.66 price; therefore the maximum possible bridge adjustment cannot change the present conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify unrestricted domestic and foreign cash by jurisdiction and deduct any distribution taxes or operating cash requirement in the bridge, without changing operating owner earnings.
